caption:
🚆 France vs Germany — every train of the same day, Thursday 15 October 2026.

Same rules on both sides: long-distance and regional trains only (TGV, OUIGO, Intercités, TER vs ICE, IC, RE, RB), with S-Bahn, RER and Transilien left out. Germany ran over 25,000 trains that day, France about 8,800, on two-thirds of France's area. The curves tell the rest: French trains bunch up at rush hour (nearly 1,100 on the move at 18:45, barely 450 at noon), while Germany's clockface timetable keeps around 1,350 trains running all day.

📊 Data: DELFI e.V. via gtfs.de (CC BY 4.0) · SNCF Voyageurs GTFS (Licence Ouverte). Trains follow the real tracks (© OpenStreetMap, SNCF Réseau); positions interpolated between stops.
🌍 Relief: AWS Terrain Tiles · Natural Earth.
